analysis.title: Taiwan Weekly Kickstart: TAIEX fell 17% (28% below its Oct peak) and TPEx 23%, with margin-unwind risks elevated, short-selling limits tightened to 1% of 30-day ADV, Taiwan lowered to Marketweight
key_insights: GS lowered Taiwan from Overweight to Marketweight in its Asia regional allocation and cut its end-2027 TAIEX target to 50,000 from 57,500. The target implies close to 40% upside after this week's correction, against 40% implied volatility, so the risk-adjusted return case is weaker.
The weekly drop was TAIEX -17% and TPEx -23%. Chemicals (-24%), Hardware (-24%), Semis (others -23%, TSMC -15%) and Capital Goods (-19%) led the declines.

Foreign investors (QFIIs) net sold US$5.8bn of cash equities in the week, concentrated in TSMC (-US$3.8bn) and Commodities (-US$600mn). Short interest fell over the week. Domestic funds net sold US$660mn, mainly ex-TSMC Tech, while Dealers net bought US$2.5bn in Tech and Financials.
Retail investors stayed net buyers despite sharp margin unwinds. Taiwan-focused ETFs took in US$4.8bn: broad-market passive US$2.5bn, Dividend US$900mn, and Leveraged and Active US$700mn each.

Retail margin balances fell to US$17bn from a US$28bn peak, including a US$4.3bn drop this week. The aggregate maintenance margin ratio (MMR) is 132%, close to the 130% margin-call threshold for individual accounts. 53% of stocks (44% of ex-TSMC free float) are below the threshold, so forced-deleveraging risk is broad.
Leveraged ETF exposure is US$11bn, or 0.8% of market free float, as retail investors keep buying the dip. Leveraged ETF AUM is about US$13bn.
Short-selling limits were tightened to 1% of 30-day ADV, per the report headline.

QFIIs have sold a record US$95bn YTD, led by TSMC (-US$74bn) and other Tech (-US$25bn), partly offset by US$15bn of non-Tech buying. Foreign ownership remains elevated in Tech, while rotation into non-Tech lifted Financials and selected sectors to three-to-four-year highs in foreign ownership.
Hedge fund selling in Taiwan has accelerated since October. Hedge funds remain heavily overweight Asian Info Tech, leaving room for more de-risking if AI uncertainty and volatility rise.
Domestic liquidity is large: brokerage cash hit a record NT$4.7tn in September, with another NT$23.5tn in savings deposits as potential funding for dip-buying. Rising Tech-sector pay supports this.

Strong earnings growth (32% in 2027E and 25% in 2028E in GS's top-down forecast) is the main support. The offsets are AI-capex risk, high market concentration, premium relative valuations and elevated volatility. GS keeps Quality Tech as core exposure, complemented tactically by dividend-supported AI Diversifiers.

Tech's share of Taiwan earnings has risen from about 50% in the early 2010s to about 85% in 2027E, which raises sensitivity to AI and semiconductor fundamentals. GS expects AI capex to rise at least through 2028, but growth likely peaks in 2027 as funding, credit, regulatory and data-center constraints bind.

Valuation: MSCI Taiwan forward 12m/24m P/E is 12.7x/10.0x (-1.3/-2.2 s.d.). Tech has de-rated to about 1 s.d. below its average P/E, while Financials trade at elevated valuations (+2.2 s.d.) despite weaker earnings growth, which supports GS's domestic preference for Tech over non-Tech.
Taiwan Tech trades at a 21% P/E premium to global Tech peers (15% excluding TSMC), against historical discounts, which limits its relative appeal globally.

TAIEX implied volatility has doubled since 2023. The 3m implied vol average was 15% in 2023, 18% in 2024, 21% in 2025 and 31% in 2026YTD, while TAIEX returned 26-28% a year in 2023-2025 and +23% in 2026YTD.

3Q26 earnings review: Taiwan earnings rose 71% yoy and 6% qoq, with 36% of companies beating and 44% missing. The median earnings surprise was -2%, weighed by small caps, against a 4% median sales beat.
Consensus 2027E EPS rose 0.3% this week, led by Industrials and Tech. TSMC ADR premium fell to 11% (-1pp) and the GS reversal index GSSRTSMR is at -0.1, relatively neutral.

Macro: export orders rose 78% yoy in October (vs +62% in September). Listed company revenues grew 54% yoy in October (vs 50% in September), with October sales tracking at 35% of consensus Q4 estimates against a historical average of 33%.

The MSCI November 2026 index review rebalance takes effect at the November 30 close. Largest estimated passive inflows are Chunghwa Telecom (US$636mn) and First Financial (US$561mn). Largest outflows are Evergreen Marine (-US$1,019mn), Cathay Financial (-US$880mn) and Chailease (-US$682mn).

earnings_insights: 3Q26 Taiwan net income rose 71% yoy and 6% qoq (all companies, reported). 36% of companies beat and 44% missed consensus. The median earnings surprise was -2% and the median sales surprise +4%.
Consensus EPS growth for Taiwan (TAIEX+TPEx) is 72% for 2026E, 32% for 2027E and 27% for 2028E. GS top-down EPS growth is 32% for 2027E and 25% for 2028E. These are forecasts, not reported figures.
Consensus 2027E EPS for Taiwan rose 0.3% in the week and 2.2% over 4 weeks (consensus estimate revisions, not reported results).
October listed-company sales grew 54% yoy (reported, vs 50% in September) and were tracking at 35% of consensus Q4 estimates, against a 33% historical average.
Next earnings dates in the MSCI flow table include Mega Financial on Nov 24, Cathay Financial on Nov 27 and Hua Nan Financial on Nov 26.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Export orders accelerated from +62% in September, which supports the earnings-growth case despite the equity sell-off.
Up from 50% in September, with October sales at 35% of consensus Q4 estimates.
Growth is driven by exports and investment, with net exports adding 5.3pp in 2026E.

risk_factors: AI-capex risk: capex growth is likely to peak in 2027 as funding, credit, regulatory and data-center constraints become more binding.
High market concentration: Tech is about 85% of 2027E Taiwan earnings and TSMC is about 40% of index weight.
Forced deleveraging: aggregate MMR is near the 130% margin-call threshold and over half of stocks are below it, with leveraged ETF exposure still at US$11bn.
Elevated volatility: implied volatility of about 40% reduces the risk-adjusted return of the 40% upside to target.
Relative valuation: Taiwan Tech trades at a 21% P/E premium to global Tech peers against historical discounts.
Further foreign and hedge fund de-risking, given record QFII selling of US$95bn YTD and heavy hedge fund overweight in Asian Info Tech.
Elevated foreign ownership in Tech and elevated domestic leverage.

vol_and_positioning: TAIEX implied volatility is about 40%, double its 2023 level (3m implied vol averages: 15% in 2023, 18% in 2024, 21% in 2025, 31% in 2026YTD).

Aggregate maintenance margin ratio is 132% against the 130% margin-call threshold for individual accounts. 53% of stocks with market cap over US$500mn are below 130%, representing 44% of ex-TSMC free float. Broad-based margin calls last occurred in April 2025.
Margin balance fell to US$17bn from a US$28bn peak, and margin exposure as a share of free float remains above the August trough.
Leveraged ETF exposure is US$11bn, 0.8% of market free float, and leveraged ETFs took in about US$700mn this week.
Taiwan's short-selling limit was tightened to 1% of 30-day ADV. Short interest fell this week.

TAIFEX net open interest in index and ETF futures: foreign institutions -US$1.0bn (55th percentile), domestic retail +US$19.4bn (87th percentile), domestic funds -US$21.2bn (12th percentile), domestic dealers +US$2.7bn (78th percentile). Foreign investors added US$8.8bn of futures open interest this week while selling US$5.8bn of cash equities.
Hedge funds remain heavily overweight Asian Info Tech and Taiwan hedge fund selling accelerated since October, which leaves scope for further de-risking.
Retail (non-institutional) investors bought US$37.7bn of cash equities YTD and US$2.4bn this week. Dealers bought US$1.6bn of TSMC in the week.
Taiwan is underweight in global mutual funds by 426bp (global funds), 588bp (AeJ funds) and 275bp (GEM funds) versus the MSCI benchmark as of end October.
geopolitical: GS Cross-Strait Risk Index (GSSRCSRI) reads 72 and the Cross-Strait Risk Barometer (GSSRCSRB) reads 42, shown among the report's equity and policy risk indicators.

tension_points.bull_case: GS's 50,000 target implies close to 40% upside after the correction. Earnings growth of 32% in 2027E and 25% in 2028E, forward P/E at -1.3 s.d. and large domestic liquidity (record NT$4.7tn brokerage cash) support dip-buying.
tension_points.bear_case: AI capex growth likely peaks in 2027, the market is concentrated in Tech, Taiwan Tech trades at a 21% premium to global peers, and implied volatility of 40% erodes the risk-adjusted return. Foreign ownership and domestic leverage remain elevated.
tension_points.what_invalidates: AI capex growth peaking in 2027 as funding, credit, regulatory and data-center constraints become more binding.

tension_points.bull_case: Retail and ETF buying has absorbed record foreign selling, and margin balances have already fallen to US$17bn from US$28bn.
tension_points.bear_case: Aggregate MMR of 132% sits close to the 130% margin-call threshold with 53% of stocks below it, and leveraged ETF exposure is still US$11bn, so forced deleveraging could extend the decline.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The aggregate MMR falling below the 130% margin-call threshold.
